{{nihongo|'''Tachibana Shrine'''|橘樹神社 (茂原市)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kazusa Province]].

'''Tachibana Shrine''' (たちばなじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in Honno, {{ill|Mobara|Q502486|qid=Q502486}}, {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|Q80011|qid=Q80011}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} and the {{ill|Kazusa Province|Q1055394|qid=Q1055394}} {{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379|lt=Ninomiya}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=former shrine rank system}} it was a {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=kensha|qid=Q90139226}}. Its shrine crest is the "tachibana" citrus.

In older records it was also written "Tachibana Jinja" and "Tachibaki Jinja." Today, the two characters "橘樹" are read "Tachibana."

== Enshrined deities ==
'''Main deity'''
* '''{{ill|Tachibanahime-no-Mikoto|Q11487396|qid=Q11487396|lt=Ototachibana-hime-no-Mikoto}}''' (おとたちばなひめのみこと)

'''Co-enshrined deities'''
* {{ill|Yamato Takeru|lt=Yamato Takeru|qid=Q461258}} (やまとたけるのみこと) - husband of Ototachibana-hime.
* Oshiyama no Sukune (おしやまのすくね) - father of Ototachibana-hime.

=== History ===
=== Overview ===
Shrine tradition says that during Yamato Takeru's eastern campaign, when crossing from {{ill|Sagami Province|Q1053732|qid=Q1053732|lt=Sagami}} to Kazusa and encountering a storm at sea, his consort {{ill|Tachibanahime-no-Mikoto|Q11487396|qid=Q11487396}} sacrificed herself to calm the seas. Yamato Takeru then made her tomb, enshrined her comb, and planted tachibana trees; this is said to be the origin. The ''{{ill|Kojiki|Q813031|qid=Q813031}}'' says "After seven days, her comb came ashore; they took it and made a tomb"<ref>[https://www.seisaku.bz/kojiki/kojiki_11.html Kojiki, Middle Book 4, Emperor Keiko]</ref>, and this is identified with this shrine. In the ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}}'', the related account of Yamato Takeru's sea crossing and onward route is also regarded as the origin narrative<ref>[https://www.seisaku.bz/nihonshoki/shoki_07.html Nihon Shoki, Vol.7, Emperor Keiko Chronicle]</ref>.

The first appearance in the six national histories is in ''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}'', entry for May 17, {{ill|877|Q23905|qid=Q23905}} ({{ill|Gangyō|Q747451|qid=Q747451}} 1), granting Tachibaki deity Senior Fifth Rank Lower. On July 15, {{ill|884|Q23895|qid=Q23895}} (Gangyo 8), Senior Fifth Rank Upper was granted, and Yamato Takeru and Oshiyama no Sukune were co-enshrined. In the ''{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}'' {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Register of Shrines}}, it appears in Chōsei District of Kazusa Province as "Tachi Shrine," listed as a Shikinaisha.

In the {{ill|Middle Ages|Q12554|qid=Q12554}}, the shrine possessed shrine lands called Tachibaki-no-shō (later Ninomiya-no-shō). It is said to have been granted Senior First Rank in {{ill|1681|Q7645|qid=Q7645}} ({{ill|Enpō|Q1145735|qid=Q1145735}} 8).

In {{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}} (Meiji 6), it was ranked as a {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=kensha|qid=Q90139226}} under the modern shrine ranking system.

=== Divine ranks ===
* {{ill|Gangyō|Q747451|qid=Q747451}} 1 ({{ill|877|Q23905|qid=Q23905}}), May 17: from Junior Fifth Rank Upper Merit Grade 5 to Senior Fifth Rank Lower Merit Grade 5 (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}'') - recorded as "Tachibaki deity".
* {{ill|Gangyō|Q747451|qid=Q747451}} 8 ({{ill|884|Q23895|qid=Q23895}}), July 15: Senior Fifth Rank Upper Merit Grade 5 (''Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku'') - recorded as "Tachi deity".

=== Precinct ===
The honden was built in {{ill|1800|Q6875|qid=Q6875}} ({{ill|Kansei|Q1195131|qid=Q1195131}} 12), Edo period.

Behind the honden remains a {{ill|Kofun|ca|Kofun|cs|Kofun|da|Kofun|de|Kofun|eo|Kofun|es|Kofun|fa|کوفون|fi|Kofun|fr|Kofun|he|קופון (רוגם)|hr|Kofun (grobnica)|it|Kofun|ja|古墳|ko|고훈|my|ခိုဖွန်း|pl|Kofun (kurhan)|pt|Kofun|ru|Кофун (захоронение)|simple|Kofun|th|โคฟุง|tr|Kofun|uk|Кофун|zh|古墳|qid=Q1141225}} said to be the tomb of Ototachibana-hime-no-Mikoto. Before the honden was built, worship is said to have been directed from the haiden straight toward this tumulus. The Miyazuma Pond in the precinct is traditionally said to be a pit from digging that tomb.

=== Sessha and massha ===
[[ファイル:橘樹神社 (茂原市) 摂末社.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Sessha and massha]]
All are massha.
* Akiba Shrine
** Deities: Izanami-no-Mikoto, Homusubi-no-Mikoto
*: Invited in the Tensho era.
* Kasushima Shrine
** Deity: Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto
*: Invited in the Bunroku era.
* Inari Shrine
** Deity: Ukemochi-no-Mikoto
*: Enshrined since the foundation.
* Koyasu Shrine
** Deity: Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto
*: Invited in the Eiroku era.
* Kureto Shrine
** Deity: Ame-no-Tajikarao-no-Mikoto
*: Relocated together with the fall of Honno Castle.

* Genshi Festival ({{ill|January 3|Q2156|qid=Q2156}})
* Kinen Festival ({{ill|February 17|Q2341|qid=Q2341}})
* Great summer purification ({{ill|June 30|Q2657|qid=Q2657}})
* Annual festival (day before {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Health and Sports Day}} in October) - formerly held on {{ill|October 10|Q2921|qid=Q2921}}.
* Niiname Festival ({{ill|November 23|Q3021|qid=Q3021}})
* Old talisman burning rite ({{ill|December 31|Q2912|qid=Q2912}})
* Great year-end purification ({{ill|December 21|Q2603|qid=Q2603}})

=== Cultural properties ===
=== Chiba Prefecture designated cultural property ===
* Tachibaki-sha documents (with petition and complaint documents of Hasegawa Arinori) (calligraphy) - designated March 10, 1989.

=== Mobara City designated cultural properties ===
* Honno Tachibana Shrine grove (natural monument) - designated Feb 26, 1980.
* Miyanoshita ruins (historic site) - designated Dec 28, 1978.
* Tachibana Shrine Ogiu Sorai calligraphy plaque (with Sorai's autograph "Koto no Ki") and sacred cedar (calligraphy) - designated Jan 22, 1993.
